name: Mahmoud Abbas
role: President of the State of Palestine and of the Palestinian National Authority; Chairman of the PLO Executive Committee (رئيس دولة فلسطين ورئيس السلطة الوطنية الفلسطينية)
party: Fatah (حركة التحرير الوطني الفلسطيني, Palestinian National Liberation Movement)
bio: Mahmoud Abbas (محمود عباس), also known as Abu Mazen, was born in Safed in 1935 and grew up as a refugee in Syria after the 1948 war; an early member of Fatah and a PLO negotiator who signed the 1993 Oslo Accords for the PLO, he was briefly the Palestinian Authority's first prime minister in 2003. He has chaired the PLO Executive Committee since November 2004 and has been President of the Palestinian National Authority since 15 January 2005, after winning the election of 9 January 2005 to succeed Yasser Arafat with 62.5% of the votes cast according to the Central Elections Commission; the PLO Central Council also designated him President of the State of Palestine in 2008, and he has chaired Fatah since 2009, most recently re-elected unanimously in May 2026. His four-year term expired in January 2009 and was extended by the PLO Central Council; no presidential or legislative election has been held since 2006, Hamas took control of the Gaza Strip in 2007, and he has governed by decree-law since the Legislative Council stopped meeting that year. His presidency combined the pursuit of statehood through international bodies (non-member observer state status at the UN in 2012, accession to the International Criminal Court in 2015, recognition by 157 of the 193 UN member states by September 2025) with recurring controversy over his writings and statements about the Holocaust and Jews, the cancelled 2021 elections, the death of the critic Nizar Banat in PA custody in 2021, corruption allegations and payments to the families of prisoners and of Palestinians killed in the conflict, which he abolished by decree in February 2025 in a reform whose implementation the United States and Israel dispute. In 2025 he created the post of vice-president, filled by Hussein al-Sheikh, and named him interim successor; as of 22 October 2026, aged 90, he remains in office after postponing the legislative election set for 28 November 2026 and the presidential election planned for early 2027 to 11 September 2027, citing Israeli measures; France asked him to reconsider, and Israel's foreign minister called the reasons given a 'ridiculous lie'.
